brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.

requirements.evidence: Two full bases (piece:0,0,0;full and piece:1,0,0;full), each with a full-depth open bin (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full); staged with fork, knife and spoon props standing in the bins. The bins are solid/non-drained, so they do not leak by design other than print porosity.
Exactly two bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full, one per base cell.

The configurator checks fit/collisions only and knows nothing about materials, waterproofing or print porosity; the parts are 3D printed in a material the user chooses. The solid (non-drained) bin shape helps, but waterproofness cannot be verified or claimed here.

finish.summary: Built a compact two-bin utensil holder: two joined full hex bases, each holding a solid full-depth bin (chosen non-drained to best approach holding water), capped open faces and locked joints, staged with fork/knife in one bin and a spoon in the other. Check is clear. Waterproof and dishwasher-safe could not be met/claimed: those depend on the user's chosen 3D-print material and print quality, which the configurator does not assess.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
